correctness.rationale: A complete infinite proof: (i) spoke colours at inner triangles are permutations; in a two-equal outer cut the repeated and missing colours exchange at each column, impossible for odd k under cyclic closure; (ii) for odd k every two-colour cut has two strands whose cyclic order reverses at each of k triangle columns, so the monodromy is a transposition and their two-factor is Hamiltonian; (iii) for even k triangle contraction yields a cubic bipartite graph with two even-size parts and preserves bichromatic component counts, while the product of signs of three relative Hamiltonian-matching permutations contradicts the identity. Explicitly treats k>=1. Two independent programs enumerate normalised factorisations k<=8 and k<=10 and inspect all bichromatic components; their actual execution outputs agree with prior Jacobsthal enumeration and the claimed dichotomy. Their finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A natural outstanding structural question after a 2011 existence theorem and 2015 exhaustive count is which known one-factorizations are perfect. The answer is a sharp all-k parity classification, and on odd k proves an unusually strong universal Hamiltonicity of all exponentially many edge-colorings; on even k it proves impossibility although 4J(k) proper colorings exist. The Kempe consequence gives an exact rigidity distinction beyond the total counting theorem and is not an arbitrary small finite computation.
